what: item 1: is the 262K decode drop 0.1.43.1 -> 0.1.45 real? Same workload, args and env, both binaries

window.gates: MemAvailable 69,297 MiB; VRAM 2,214 MiB; 8081 restored healthy after ~24 s

workload: 261,888-token prompt, --max-context 262144, 64 new tokens; production env (SELECT_WMMA, HIP_WMMA, SH_STREAM, TAIL_SKIP=7, lookup-chain 2, spec 5, kv-resident 32768, prefill 8192)

pairs.note: the 0143 cell is a stall/outlier (ms/round 53.9 vs 38.7-39.1 in the other pairs); excluded from the reading, kept in the record

median.note: median over the three pairs as run; the two clean pairs are +2.70% and +3.96%

prefill.reading: 0.1.45 is also ~3% faster in prefill on the same config

reading: 0.1.45 is FASTER at 262K on the same config (+3.96% median decode, +3% prefill). The 69.3-vs-56.5 gap is CONFIG/METHODOLOGY, not a line regression: the R1292 sweep config differs (its 69.3 cannot be reproduced on 0.1.43.1 with the current production env and a 64-token cell).
disposition: the suspected deep-tier regression is CLOSED as config-dependent; the ledger's 262K row should quote 56.5 tok/s for this config and stop citing 69.3 as a like-for-like prior. No adoption, production untouched.
